passages.text: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD became angry with Israel again.
The LORD’s anger burned against Israel.
The LORD caused David to act against Israel.
The LORD moved David to take action.
The LORD told David, “Go and count the people of Israel and Judah.”
David was told to take a census of Israel and Judah.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙סֶף֙ אַף־ יְהוָ֔ה לַחֲר֖וֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֨סֶת אֶת־ דָּוִ֤ד בָּהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֛ךְ מְנֵ֥ה אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶת־ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Joab.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab was with David at that time.
David gave Joab a command.
David said, “Go through all the tribes of Israel.”
He said, “Start at Dan.”
He said, “Go as far as Beersheba.”
He said, “Count all the people.”
He said, “I want to know the number of the people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֣ב׀ שַׂר־ הַחַ֣יִל אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֗וֹ שֽׁוּט־ נָ֞א בְּכָל־ שִׁבְטֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע וּפִקְד֖וּ אֶת־ הָעָ֑ם וְיָ֣דַעְתִּ֔י אֵ֖ת מִסְפַּ֥ר הָעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”
passages.sermon:
Joab spoke to King David.
Joab said, “May the LORD your God increase the people.
May the LORD make them a hundred times more than they are now.
May my lord the king see this with his own eyes.
But why does my lord the king desire to do this thing?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹאָ֜ב אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיוֹסֵ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֶל־ הָעָ֜ם כָּהֵ֤ם׀ וְכָהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים וְעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ רֹא֑וֹת וַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֥מָּה חָפֵ֖ץ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to count the troops of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The king was David.
David gave a command.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
There were other commanders with Joab.
Joab and the commanders did not agree with David’s command.
David’s command was stronger than their objections.
David’s word prevailed over Joab and the commanders.
Joab and the commanders obeyed David.
Joab and the commanders left David’s presence.
Joab and the commanders went out to count the people of Israel.
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב וְעַ֖ל שָׂרֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיֵּצֵ֨א יוֹאָ֜ב וְשָׂרֵ֤י הַחַ֙יִל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִפְקֹ֥ד אֶת־ הָעָ֖ם אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.
passages.sermon:
Joab and the commanders of the army left the king.
They crossed the Jordan River.
They camped near Aroer.
Aroer is south of the town.
The town is in the middle of the valley.
They went toward Gad.
They went toward Jazer.
passages.original: וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בַעֲרוֹעֵ֗ר יְמִ֥ין הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּתוֹךְ־ הַנַּ֥חַל הַגָּ֖ד וְאֶל־ יַעְזֵֽר׃

passages.text: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.
passages.sermon:
Joab and the commanders of the army traveled through the land of Israel.
They went to Gilead.
They went to the land of Tahtim-hodshi.
They went to Dan-jaan.
They went around to Sidon.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔דָה וְאֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֖ים חָדְשִׁ֑י וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ דָּ֣נָה יַּ֔עַן וְסָבִ֖יב אֶל־ צִידֽוֹן׃

passages.text: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
passages.sermon:
Joab and his men traveled through the land.
They went to the fortress of Tyre.
They visited all the cities of the Hivites.
They visited all the cities of the Canaanites.
They continued to the Negev region in Judah.
They reached Beersheba.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ מִבְצַר־ צֹ֔ר וְכָל־ עָרֵ֥י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י וַיֵּֽצְא֛וּ אֶל־ נֶ֥גֶב יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

passages.text: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: Joab and his men traveled through the whole land.\r\nThey spent nine months and twenty days on their journey.\r\nThey returned to Jerusalem at the end of this time.
passages.original: וַיָּשֻׁ֖טוּ בְּכָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ מִקְצֵ֨ה תִשְׁעָ֧ה חֳדָשִׁ֛ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים י֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of the army.
Joab gave the total number of the people to the king.
In Israel, there were 800,000 strong men.
These men could fight with the sword.
In Judah, there were 500,000 men.
These men could also fight.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־ מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד־ הָעָ֖ם אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתְּהִ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שְׁמֹנֶה֩ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֤לֶף אִֽישׁ־ חַ֙יִל֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה חֲמֵשׁ־ מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David counted the people of Israel.
After David counted the people, his heart troubled him.
David realized he had done wrong.
David spoke to the LORD.
David said, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done.”
David asked the LORD to forgive his sin.
David said, “O LORD, please take away the guilt of Your servant.”
David admitted, “I have acted very foolishly.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֤ךְ לֵב־ דָּוִד֙ אֹת֔וֹ אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֖ן סָפַ֣ר אֶת־ הָעָ֑םס וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ יְהוָ֗ה חָטָ֤אתִי מְאֹד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה הַֽעֲבֶר־ נָא֙ אֶת־ עֲוֺ֣ן עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֥י נִסְכַּ֖לְתִּי מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: When David got up in the morning, a revelation from the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Gad was a prophet.
Gad was also David’s seer.
David got up in the morning.
The LORD spoke to Gad.
The LORD gave Gad a message for David.
The LORD said, “Go and speak to David.”
The LORD said, “This is what I say.”
The LORD said, “I am giving you three choices.”
The LORD said, “Choose one of these options.”
The LORD said, “I will do the one you choose.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֥קָם דָּוִ֖ד בַּבֹּ֑קֶר פ וּדְבַר־ יְהוָ֗ה הָיָה֙ אֶל־ גָּ֣ד הַנָּבִ֔יא חֹזֵ֥ה דָוִ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר׃ הָל֞וֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁלֹ֕שׁ אָנֹכִ֖י נוֹטֵ֣ל עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר־ לְךָ֥ אַֽחַת־ מֵהֶ֖ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
passages.sermon:
Gad was a prophet.
Gad came to David.
Gad spoke to David.
Gad gave David a message from the LORD.
Gad asked David a question.
Gad said, “Will you have seven years of famine in your land?”
Gad said, “Or will you flee from your enemies for three months, while they pursue you?”
Gad said, “Or will there be three days of plague in your land?”
Gad told David to consider these choices.
Gad told David to decide what answer he should give to the One who sent him.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא־ גָ֥ד אֶל־ דָּוִ֖ד וַיַּגֶּד־ ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡וֹ הֲתָב֣וֹא לְךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֣ים׀ רָעָ֣ב׀ בְּאַרְצֶ֡ךָ אִם־ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְךָ֨ לִפְנֵֽי־ צָרֶ֜יךָ וְה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗ךָ וְאִם־ הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֙בֶר֙ בְּאַרְצֶ֔ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּרְאֵ֔ה מָה־ אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר׃ס

passages.text: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Gad was a prophet and David’s seer.
David spoke to Gad.
David said, “I am in great distress.”
David said, “Let us fall into the hand of the LORD.”
David said, “The LORD has great mercy.”
David said, “Do not let me fall into the hand of men.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־ גָּ֖ד צַר־ לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְּלָה־ נָּ֤א בְיַד־ יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ רַבִּ֣ים רַחֲמוֹ וּבְיַד־ אָדָ֖ם אַל־ אֶפֹּֽלָה׃

passages.text: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sent a plague on Israel.
The plague began in the morning.
The plague lasted until the appointed time.
Seventy thousand people died.
These people died from Dan to Beersheba.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה דֶּ֙בֶר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵהַבֹּ֖קֶר וְעַד־ עֵ֣ת מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיָּ֣מָת מִן־ הָעָ֗ם מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem.
The angel intended to destroy Jerusalem.
The LORD saw this.
The LORD changed his mind about bringing disaster.
The LORD spoke to the angel who was destroying the people.
The LORD said, "Enough! Stop now!"
At that time, the angel of the LORD stood by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יָד֨וֹ הַמַּלְאָ֥ךְ׀ יְרֽוּשָׁלִַם֮ לְשַׁחֲתָהּ֒ וַיִּנָּ֤חֶם יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַ֠יֹּאמֶר לַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַמַּשְׁחִ֤ית בָּעָם֙ רַ֔ב עַתָּ֖ה הֶ֣רֶף יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ הָיָ֔ה עִם־ גֹּ֖רֶן הָאוֹרְנָה הַיְבֻסִֽי׃ס

passages.text: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David saw the angel.
The angel was striking down the people of Israel.
David spoke to the LORD.
David said, “I have sinned.”
David said, “I have done wrong.”
David said, “I am the shepherd.”
David said, “These people are like sheep.”
David said, “What have these sheep done?”
David said, “Let Your hand be against me.”
David said, “Let Your hand be against my father’s house.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־ יְהוָ֜ה בִּרְאֹת֣וֹ׀ אֶֽת־ הַמַּלְאָ֣ךְ׀ הַמַּכֶּ֣ה בָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֤י חָטָ֙אתִי֙ וְאָנֹכִ֣י הֶעֱוֵ֔יתִי וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א יָדְךָ֛ בִּ֖י וּבְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי׃פ

passages.text: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
passages.sermon:
Gad was a prophet of the LORD.
David was the king of Israel.
On that day, Gad came to David.
Gad spoke to David.
Gad said, “Go up to the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
Build an altar there to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא־ גָ֥ד אֶל־ דָּוִ֖ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ עֲלֵה֙ הָקֵ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּגֹ֖רֶן אָרָנְיָה הַיְבֻסִֽי׃

passages.text: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Gad was a prophet of the LORD.
The LORD gave a command to David through Gad.
Gad spoke the LORD’s command to David.
David obeyed the LORD’s command.
David went up as Gad told him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִד֙ כִּדְבַר־ גָּ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.
passages.sermon:
Araunah was a Jebusite.  
Araunah looked out.  
He saw the king.  
He saw the king’s servants.  
They were coming toward him.  
Araunah went out to meet them.  
He bowed down before the king.  
He put his face to the ground.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֣ף אֲרַ֗וְנָה וַיַּ֤רְא אֶת־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְאֶת־ עֲבָדָ֔יו עֹבְרִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֲרַ֔וְנָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said. “To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
passages.sermon:
Araunah saw King David coming.
Araunah spoke to David.
Araunah said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?”
David answered Araunah.
David said, “I have come to buy your threshing floor.”
David said, “I want to build an altar to the LORD.”
David said, “I want the plague to stop among the people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲרַ֔וְנָה מַדּ֛וּעַ בָּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לִקְנ֧וֹת מֵעִמְּךָ֣ אֶת־ הַגֹּ֗רֶן לִבְנ֤וֹת מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Araunah said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
passages.sermon:
Araunah spoke to David.
Araunah saw that David was the king.
Araunah said, “My lord the king may take what he wants.
You may offer it as a sacrifice.
Here are the oxen for a burnt offering.
Here are the threshing sledges.
Here are the ox yokes for the wood.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֙וְנָה֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד יִקַּ֥ח וְיַ֛עַל אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינוֹ רְאֵה֙ הַבָּקָ֣ר לָעֹלָ֔ה וְהַמֹּרִגִּ֛ים וּכְלֵ֥י הַבָּקָ֖ר לָעֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: O king, Araunah gives all these to the king.” He also said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
passages.sermon:
Araunah was a Jebusite.
Araunah owned a threshing floor in Jerusalem.
David was the king of Israel.
Araunah spoke to King David.
Araunah said, “O king, I give everything to you.”
Araunah gave the oxen, the threshing floor, and the tools to David.
Araunah also said to David, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
passages.original: הַכֹּ֗ל נָתַ֛ן אֲרַ֥וְנָה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְס וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֙וְנָה֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִרְצֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Araunah offered to give David the threshing floor and oxen for free.
David spoke to Araunah.
David said, “No.”
David said, “I will buy them from you for a price.”
David said, “I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing.”
David bought the threshing floor and the oxen from Araunah.
David paid fifty shekels of silver.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־ אֲרַ֗וְנָה לֹ֚א כִּֽי־ קָנ֨וֹ אֶקְנֶ֤ה מֵאֽוֹתְךָ֙ בִּמְחִ֔יר וְלֹ֧א אַעֲלֶ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י עֹל֣וֹת חִנָּ֑ם וַיִּ֨קֶן דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־ הַגֹּ֙רֶן֙ וְאֶת־ הַבָּקָ֔ר בְּכֶ֖סֶף שְׁקָלִ֥ים חֲמִשִּֽׁים׃

passages.text: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David built an altar to the LORD at that place.
David offered burnt offerings to the LORD.
David also offered peace offerings to the LORD.
The LORD heard the prayers for the land.
The LORD stopped the plague in Israel.
passages.original: וַיִּבֶן֩ שָׁ֨ם דָּוִ֤ד מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַל עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיֵּעָתֵ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ וַתֵּעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
